title: Balance pass, three heroes each, draft-style hero select
problem: The owner asked to do the balance tuning first, to give each player 3 heroes, and to make the hero selection screen feel like the draft and character-select screens of fighting and MOBA games.
scope: Balance pass first: species, heroes, pace of play, economy; measured with large bot-vs-bot runs; numbers in rules.ts and hero kits
Three heroes per player: draft, start on the map one per lane, three HUD panels, shop tabs, bot and economy
Draft-style hero select: turns with the bot, two facing rows of slots, big hero preview on a stage, roster grid of portraits, picked heroes taken
Versus loading screen with both line-ups and species before the match
Re-check balance after the third hero, re-tune if needed; tests, docs, records

acceptance.text: Balance: over 400 bot matches each species wins 40-60%, each hero 35-65%; draws under 15%; few matches decided before 2:30
acceptance.evidence: npm run balance (1,200 bot matches, 3 heroes a side): species 47-58% (Kampung 49, Hutan 50, Sungai 47, Serangga 47, Batu 58); heroes 42-62%; draws 8%; decided before 2:30 under 1%; average 5:00. Before tuning (400 matches): Dalang 85%, Batu 71%, Kampung 29%, early finishes 8%. Ran on 1,200 matches instead of 400 because 400 swung up to 10 points between runs.

acceptance.text: Three heroes each: picks validated (3, no duplicates across sides), start one per lane, all usable (automated)
acceptance.evidence: orders.test.ts: three heroes start one per lane (2-lane mode: third joins the left lane); picks always 3 with no hero on both sides; draft helper test. All hero, map, fog, species and rules tests moved to 3-hero line-ups (84/84).

acceptance.text: Draft: turn order, bot picks avoid taken heroes and replay exactly; versus screen then match starts with the drafted line-ups (browser check)
acceptance.evidence: orders.test.ts: bot draft picks never take a taken hero, repeat exactly for the same inputs, and give the bot three different jobs. phone-check: species -> draft (turns you 1, bot 2, you 2, bot 1) -> versus screen -> match starts with exactly the drafted line-ups, no overlap.

acceptance.text: Same seed + same moves = same match; soak passes with 3 heroes
acceptance.evidence: tests/determinism.test.ts 4/4 with 3 random heroes a side; npm run soak 100 + 20 matches, no errors; every hero and species played.

acceptance.text: Phone-size browser check: draft, versus screen, 3 hero panels, no page errors
acceptance.evidence: node scripts/phone-check.cjs (iPhone 13 size): species, draft, versus, 3 hero panels, wave chip, Farm/Ward/Move, shop, ULT call and fire, full match, 2 lanes; PHONE CHECK OK, no page errors; screenshots checked.
Not yet tried on the owner's phone.

acceptance.text: Owner's verdict: fair-feeling matches? draft exciting? 3 heroes manageable?

risks: Bot-vs-bot balance is a proxy: it measures the bot's play, not people's
Three heroes may be a lot to manage on a phone
The order of work: balance is tuned first, then re-checked after the third hero, because a third hero shifts the numbers
cost: RM0. Free tools; private preview page. Several build sessions (estimate).
userNotes: Balance pass: species and heroes evened out (every species now wins 47-58% against the bot, every hero 42-62%), fewer draws and no more very early finishes.
Fixed: towers now shoot back at long-range attackers that used to hit them from just outside their reach.
Sudden death: towers take triple damage, so a level match is decided more often.
Three heroes each, drafted in turns with the bot on a new hero-select screen, then a versus screen before the match.

approval.evidence: do all the balance tunes first, each character should select 3 heroes, the loading screen where you select heroes should be like dota/tekken
